concepts.question: Does the cell in the centre of the image contain a nucleus, that is a distinct darker internal body, or is the whole cell body uniform with no nucleus at all?

absent.text: the cell body is one even mass throughout, with no darker internal patch standing out from the rest

present.text: a distinctly darker, sharply bounded internal body sits inside the cell and contrasts with the paler cytoplasm

concepts.question: How large is the central cell compared with the surrounding red blood cells: clearly smaller than one red cell, about the same size, or clearly larger?

much_smaller.text: the cell spans about a quarter of a neighbouring red cell, near 2 um across

similar.text: the cell matches a nearby red cell in width to within about a fifth of that width

larger.text: the cell is plainly wider than every red cell around it, up to about twice a red cell across

concepts.question: What is the shape of the nucleus: no nucleus at all, a single round or oval mass, a single indented, kidney-shaped or band-like mass, two lobes joined by a strand, or three or more lobes joined by thin strands?

none.text: the cell carries no internal outline at all, so neither a lobe nor an indentation can be sought

round.text: a single unbroken circular or oval mass with a smooth convex edge and no notch in it

indented.text: one mass whose edge is notched, kidney- or band-shaped, the notch cutting less than half way across

bilobed.text: two rounded segments of similar size joined by a single narrow thread of chromatin

multilobed.text: three to five rounded segments strung in a chain, each joined to the next by a thin thread

concepts.question: How dense is the nuclear material: there is no nuclear material at all, open and finely textured with pale areas, moderately clumped, densely clumped but with a visible coarse pattern of light and dark, or so uniformly dark and structureless that no internal pattern can be seen at all?

no_nucleus.text: the cell holds no nuclear material anywhere, so there is no interior texture to judge for density

open_fine.text: the nuclear interior is mostly pale with an even fine stipple and no dark clump larger than a dot

moderately_clumped.text: dark clumps cover under about half the nuclear area and the pale gaps between them stay plainly visible

dense_clumped.text: coarse violet clumps cover most of the nucleus, leaving only thin pale seams between them

pyknotic_structureless.text: the nucleus reads as one uniformly dark blot in which no lighter area or pattern can be made out

concepts.question: About what fraction of the cell area is nucleus: none of it, because there is no nucleus, less than a third (low), between a third and two thirds (moderate), or more than two thirds (high)?

no_nucleus.text: no nuclear area is present to measure, so the cell body reads as cytoplasm from edge to edge

low.text: cytoplasm forms a broad rim and the nucleus covers less than a third of the cell area

moderate.text: the nucleus covers between a third and two thirds of the cell, with a clear rim of cytoplasm all round

high.text: the nucleus fills more than two thirds of the cell and cytoplasm survives only as a thin crescent

concepts.question: What colour is the cytoplasm around the nucleus: pink or almost colourless, pale grey-blue, plainly blue, or deep intense blue?

pink_or_colourless.text: the cytoplasm is pink or almost clear, no bluer than the red cells lying around the cell

pale_grey_blue.text: a faint grey-blue wash, bluer than the red cells but much paler than the nucleus

blue.text: an even mid-blue read at a glance, clearly stronger than a grey wash but lighter than the nucleus

deep_blue.text: an intense navy blue nearly as dark as the nucleus, the strongest blue anywhere in the frame

concepts.question: How prominent are granules, that is small discrete dots, in the cytoplasm: none visible, fine and sparse or dust-like, or coarse and abundant so that they fill the cytoplasm?

absent.text: the cytoplasm is smooth and even, showing no discrete dots against its own colour

fine_sparse.text: dots are dust-like and not separately countable, so the cytoplasm looks faintly textured rather than dotted

coarse_abundant.text: dots are separately countable at the cell edge and pack the cytoplasm so that little clear ground shows

concepts.question: If granules are visible, what colour are they, from palest to darkest: none visible, pale lilac or neutral, orange-red, or dark purple to black?

none_visible.text: no dots of any colour stand out from the even tint of the cytoplasm

pale_neutral.text: dots are pale lilac or grey, barely different in hue from the cytoplasm carrying them

orange_red.text: dots are plainly orange to red, warmer than the cytoplasm and than the violet of the nucleus

dark_purple.text: dots are dark purple to nearly black, darker than the nucleus they frequently lie across

concepts.question: Do the cytoplasmic granules lie over the nucleus and hide it: not at all, partly, or so completely that the nuclear outline cannot be traced?

absent.text: every part of the nuclear outline can be followed; the dots lie beside the nucleus, not across it

partial.text: dots cross the nucleus and blur one stretch of its edge, while the remainder stays traceable

marked.text: dots cover the nucleus so densely that no stretch of its outline can be followed at all
